messages.subject: Fixing Legend
parts:
Dear All,
Please consider the simple example below.
I am having problems with the legend i.e. the two symbols shown are a
superposition of line+shape 13 (for point) and line + shape 3, whereas I
would like line+point shape 3 and line + point shape 13.
Can anyone help me out to fix my plot?
Furthermore, can I relocate the legend somewhere else? It looks to me
that it is 'stealing' space from the rest of the figure whereas it could
stay below the two lines.
Many thanks

Lorenzo

ml <- data.frame(l=1:100, one_two_separate=(1:100)*2)
ml_rew <- data.frame(l=1:100, one_two_separate=(1:100)*3)


gpl <- ggplot(ml,aes(x=l,y=one_two_separate
))+geom_line(aes(color="Aggregated"))+
# scale_x_continuous(limits=c(1,10))+
geom_point(data=ml,aes(x=l,y=one_two_separate,color="Aggregated" ),
shape=3)+
geom_point(data=ml_rew,aes(x=l,y=one_two_separate,color="Average on
30\n Rewired Networks" ), shape =13)+
geom_line(data=ml_rew,aes(x=l,y=one_two_separate, color="Average on
30\n Rewired Networks" ))+
scale_colour_hue("Network")+
xlab(expression(paste("l")))+
ylab(expression(paste("M(l)/M(",infinity,")")))+
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 20))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray", hjust=1))


fn <- paste("M_l_plot_ggplot2.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(gpl)
dev.off()

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: Fixing Legend
parts:
This is harder than I expected. I tried a few things, came across
what may be a bug (I'll have to let Hadley tell me if I am off base,
which is quite possible), and have a way to get it to work the way you
have set it up, and then I'll show you the way that is more like how
ggplot is expecting things to work (on the idea that fighting the
tools is not the easiest way to go).

I'm going to ignore all the xlab/ylab/opts statements since they
aren't related to the problem.

What I thought might work would be to put the shape declarations into
the aes() function on the idea that they were not showing up properly
on the legend because they did not actually belong to a scale, but
that gave the same result you had: the legend was differentiated by
color but had all of the line (horizontal), point 3 (plus), and point
13 (circle cross) in each the entries. Then I thought I'd be even
more explicit and add a scale_shape_identity("Network", legend=TRUE),
but that gave the same result. Even with shape in the aes(), I don't
think a shape scale is getting created. I can't tell if that is
appropriate or not.

To force the creation of a shape scale, set the shape to a string (for
convenience, the same as colour), and then manually map that to shape:

lbls <- c("Aggregated","Average on 30\n Rewired Networks")
brks <- c("A","R")

ggplot(ml, aes(x=l, y=one_two_separate)) +
geom_line(aes(colour="A")) +
geom_point(aes(colour="A", shape="A")) +
geom_line(data=ml_rew, aes(colour="R")) +
geom_point(data=ml_rew, aes(colour="R", shape="R")) +
scale_colour_discrete("Network", breaks=brks, labels=lbls) +
scale_shape_manual("Network", breaks=brks, labels=lbls, values=c
(3,13))

However, that is still somewhat fighting against the way ggplot
works. Easier is to make a single long data.frame with all the data,
each set identified by another variable:

ml_tmp <- rbind(transform(ml, set="Aggregated"),
transform(ml_rew, set="Average on 30\n Rewired Networks"))

Then the following should work, but doesn't quite (scales are not
combined) (why?):

ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=l, y=one_two_separate, colour=set, shape=set)) +
geom_point() +
geom_line() +
scale_colour_hue("Network") +
scale_shape_manual("Network", values=c(3,13))

But this (explicitly setting the breaks and labels in both the colour
and shape scale) does:

lbls <- levels(ml_tmp$set)

ggplot(ml_tmp, aes(x=l, y=one_two_separate, colour=set, shape=set)) +
geom_point() +
geom_line() +
scale_colour_hue("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls) +
scale_shape_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c
(3,13))

--Brian Diggs
